<br>

## Hamster in Your Head

<br>
If you hold this poem\
in the rain\
its fur will get soaking wet.\
If you hold this poem\
in the sun\
it will squint its eyes.\
If you hold this poem\
while you laugh\
it will wiggle its whiskers with delight.\
If you hold this poem\
with a friend\
it may warm both your hearts.\
If you read this poem\
with an open mind\
it may scurry home\
inside your head,\
with all its soaking and squinting,\
wiggling and warming,\
nestled snug\
in the sawdust\
of your childhood memories\
and the shredded paper\
of your past loves.\

`r end_poem_mark`

*Notes:* 
This poem is intended as a simple invitation to poetry for the poem-curious. 
The imagined audience of the poem was people at a coffee shop who might pick up from the countertop a paper flyer titled "Poetry to the People" distributed by Terry Sloan.
The poem is supposed to illustrate a few of the things poetry can do, in a compact and accessible stanza: 
<br>*Personification:* The poem is a person (well, a hamster, but pet hamsters do have personalities).
<br>*Metaphor:* For example, "the sawdust of childhood memories", and "the shredded paper of past loves."
<br>*Concrete bodily imagery:* Hold the furry poem and let it scurry into your head; etc.
<br>Attention to *the sounds of words,* for example the alliteration in "soaking and squinting," and "wiggling and warming."
<br>And, the poem concludes with some *classic poetic themes* of loss and nostalgia.
